business_model.claim: Easterly is an internally managed REIT that earns rent by leasing Class A commercial properties mainly to U.S. Government agencies, directly or through the GSA. The 10-K puts this at approximately 90% of revenue, and the latest 10-Q says over 85%.
quotes: We generate approximately 90% of our revenue by leasing our properties to such agencies either directly or through the U.S. General Services Administration (“GSA”).
We generate over 85% of our revenue by leasing our properties to such agencies, either directly or through the U.S. General Services Administration (“GSA”).

business_model.claim: Tenant concentration is high. U.S. Government agencies were 88.1% of annualized lease income at the last fiscal year-end. Three agencies (VA, FBI and Drug Enforcement Administration) together were about 47.3% of annualized lease income and 42.0% of leased square feet.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, our U.S. Government tenant agencies accounted for 88.1% of our annualized lease income.

business_model.claim: Revenue is almost all rent. In the year-to-date period of the latest 10-Q, rental income was 268,287 (table in thousands) of total revenues of 277,573. The rest came from tenant reimbursements of 2,137, asset management income of 2,036 and other income of 5,113.

business_model.basis: the 10-K attribution is stated. Applying it to the latest period is inferred from the acquisitions and the rental income rise.
business_model.claim: Rental income grows mainly by adding properties. Year-to-date rental income was 268,287 (table in thousands) against 238,123 a year earlier. The 10-K attributes its annual rental income increase of $32.1 million primarily to acquired properties and a full period of operations from earlier purchases.
quotes: The $32.1 million increase in Rental income is primarily attributable to the three operating properties acquired since December 31, 2024 and a full period of operations from the nine operating properties acquired during the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Lease terms are long, which gives contracted rent visibility. The weighted average remaining lease term was approximately 9.5 years at the last fiscal year-end, and government leases typically have long initial terms.
quotes: the weighted average remaining lease term was approximately 9.5 years.

business_model.claim: Lease expirations and early-termination rights are the main revenue risk. Leases for about 14.7% of annualized lease income and 17.5% of square footage expire by the end of 2028. Tenants contributing about 3.9% of annualized lease income have exercisable rights to terminate early.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, leases representing approximately 14.7% of our total annualized lease income and approximately 17.5% of the square footage of the properties in our portfolio will expire by the end of 2028.

business_model.claim: Build-to-suit development and tenant-specific build-outs are a second earnings source. The company earns a construction management fee of approximately 12% of actual construction cost, and the build-outs are said to raise renewal likelihood.
quotes: typically generate a construction management fee paid by the tenant agency to us in the amount of approximately 12% of the actual cost of construction.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items. The link of the 2,036 fee line to the JV comes from the 10-K's description of asset management income.
business_model.claim: A joint venture adds two income streams: the company's share of JV income and an asset management fee. The company owns a 53% interest in the JV. Year-to-date income from the unconsolidated venture was 5,036 (table in thousands) and asset management income was 2,036.
quotes: during 2021, we formed the JV with a leading global investor to acquire a portfolio of properties, in which we own a 53% interest.

business_model.basis: stated in the statements and the 10-K MD&A. Linking the latest period to the same drivers is inferred.
business_model.claim: Costs are mostly property-level costs, depreciation, interest and G&A. business_model.basis: stated in the cited items for the 10-K period. The nine-month rise is read from the income statement.
business_model.claim: Interest cost is a key cost driver because growth is funded with external debt. Year-to-date net interest expense rose to 60,629 (table in thousands) from 56,374. We primarily use external financing to fund acquisition, development and renovation activities.
